x: Jim Heathfield took over from Collis on the second stage for the 'D' team with Bhatia running for the 'A', Shippen for the 'C' and Conway for the 'E'.

Bhatia, on his first, and we sincerely hope not his last Brighton, took over in cold, wet and dreary conditions far from suitable for his type of running and, with a very good effort, he gained one more place.

Good times were recorded by Baulch, Bhatia, Davies and Newell. These two races,followed by our own 5¾ miles road race and 3 miles yacht handicap, preceded the London to Brighton Relay for Southern clubs on October 11th and we had every reason to think we were set for a place - in actual fact we had…

Beware; Davies, Bhatia and Robinson!! The field events boys were out in force and both Percy Porter and Dave Ansell won their respective events - the hammer, with 158'10½", and the long-jump with a leap of 20'5½".

Normally our middle-distance men could have split forces but on this occasion we had Newell, Robinson, Dabbs and Radford on holiday, Davies injured and Bhatia a 'flu victim; so it was decided to concentrate our remaining forces on the only major road-relay event we tackle before the "Brighton".
Ranjit Bhatia (21.17). The usual dash along the embankment did not deter this runner from India, who had endeared himself to all with whom he has come into contact.
